machine: Apple M6, 32 GiB unified memory, macOS 27.0
method: Each local system alone on the machine, one request at a time, with the settings of its quality run but one slot: one load, one discarded warm-up request, then three repetitions of the same 30 sentences and 30 passages, alternating. Seconds are end to end per successful item, pooled over the three repetitions (median and 90th percentile, inclusive linear interpolation). Each system was measured alone; a run starts only under the benchmark's measurement conditions (start_conditions_met), and a repetition during which they were not met is flagged and kept (flagged, one boolean per repetition). These are published measurements: verify checks their schema and ranges and recomputes the speed subsets, but cannot recompute the times or memory from the item rows.

selection.rule: Within each direction, items are ordered by SHA-256 of the UTF-8 seed string followed by the item id; the system's directions are taken in lexicographic order of their historical codes, one item from each in turn, until each type has 30 items. The seed string is historical.

caveats: Speed comes from this separate benchmark, not from the quality runs, whose timing is not a result.
Peak memory is measured on a 32 GiB machine and does not say whether a system runs comfortably on a smaller one.

Cloud references are the pilot's batched requests through the vendors' subscription clients (DeepL API through DeepL's translation API), including client start-up; they are not like-for-like API latency or cost.
Estimated cost uses API list prices on November 20, 2026 and the token counts the clients reported (tokens_per_item includes each client's own instructions); DeepL API's cost is not estimated.
